conventions.convention: Inner products are linear in the first argument. On the product domains, the commutator pairing equals −2i times the imaginary part of the centered pairing.
Strong spectral commutation means that every spectral projection of A commutes with every spectral projection of B. A commutator identity on a dense invariant domain is a different condition.

Preparation variance and spread are defined only when the outcome law has finite mean and second moment; they are not extended by infinity. Variance has the squared observable unit, and spread has the observable unit.

The Q-P product-domain intersection consists of L² classes for which D_j f, x_j f and x_j D_j f all belong to L², componentwise. The full preparation bound instead assumes only a unit vector in D(Q_j) ∩ D(P_j).

A joint sharp observable is a regular PVM on the Borel sets of R² with the exact two spectral marginals. The ideal joint instrument uses finite Borel partitions; conditional states and repeatability are asserted only for positive-probability joint bins.
The spectral constructions explicitly assume AC and Countable Choice. Physical bounds are conditional model deductions; preparation spread is distinct from apparatus error and disturbance.

load_bearing.statement: For an assigned sharp observable and a preparation with finite mean and second moment, preparation variance is the centered second moment of its outcome law and preparation spread is its nonnegative square root.

Under AC and Countable Choice, strongly commuting self-adjoint A,B on a nonzero complex Hilbert space satisfy f(A)g(B)=g(B)f(A) for bounded Borel f,g; bounded f(B) preserves D(A) and commutes with A there.

Under AC and Countable Choice, strong spectral commutation, existence of a regular joint PVM with rectangle values E_A(Λ)E_B(Σ) and the stated marginals, and commutation of all bounded Borel functions are equivalent. The joint PVM is unique and represents f(A)g(B) by the joint integral.
Under AC and Countable Choice, every nonzero ψ in D(Q_j) ∩ D(P_j) admits unit product-domain vectors converging to ψ/‖ψ‖ together with their Q_j and P_j images.

Under P1, P2, AC and Countable Choice, assigned sharp observables satisfy the weak preparation-spread bound for unit vectors in both domains; on both product domains they satisfy the Robertson bound and anticommutator refinement, with the stated refined equality criterion.

Under P1, P2, P5, P6, AC and Countable Choice, every unit ψ in D(Q_j) ∩ D(P_j) of the massive spin-s model satisfies ΔψQ_j ΔψP_j ≥ ħ/2. The centered pairing has imaginary part −ħ/2; equality holds exactly when the centered vectors are linearly dependent and their pairing has zero real part.

Under P1, P2, P3, AC and Countable Choice, compatibility is equivalent to strong spectral commutation; the unique joint PVM supplies a probability law with the individual marginals, and finite-bin ideal Lüders measurements have order-independent joint probabilities, conditional states and positive-probability repeatability.

concerns.concern: Proof 1.1 says the definitions are 'exactly the conditions of [F2]', but the local definition requires only the two marginals, whereas F2 also requires rectangle values H(Λ×Σ)=E_A(Λ)E_B(Σ). The missing implication follows immediately from PVM multiplicativity, explicitly available in F3. State that implication before invoking the criterion.

Proof 2.1 invokes '[F1] applied to the assigned sharp observable with projection-valued measure H on B(R²)'. The assigned-sharp-observable definition concerns real-valued self-adjoint operators and PVMs on R. H is instead the locally defined joint sharp observable. The general-measurable-space density/PVM probability lemma, already included in F1, directly proves the claimed law; the application should name that supplier rather than type H as an ordinary assigned sharp observable.

alerts.finding: The final 'No joint law' remark says: 'Nothing in this theorem asserts a joint outcome law of two different components S_n and S_n′ with n not parallel to n′; the incompatibility of the components is a separate result of the uncertainty page'. This item's Statement permits s=0 as well as positive spin. The uncertainty page proves incompatibility only for the three coordinate components at s=1/2 in texp-nrqm-uncertainty-spin-half-incompatibility. It does not supply the general directional claim. At s=0 all S_n are zero, so their spectral PVMs commute and a joint sharp observable exists. The unqualified incompatibility attribution therefore needs a scope restriction or a separately proved positive-spin directional result.
